newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African sheep farmers replace workers with dogs.
newsitem.headline: S.African sheep farmers replace workers with dogs.

text.p: South African sheep farmers are replacing human workers with dogs because of labour problems and fears of post-apartheid land ownership legislation, agricultural union officials said on Tuesday.
They said a draft bill on security of tenure would make it more difficult for farmers, most of them white, to evict landless people, most of them black.

"Wool farmers are turning to mutton production, they say they want to farm with one labourer and three sheepdogs," Chris du Toit, head of the South African Agricultural Union (SAAU), told reporters. "They want to get rid of labour."
Pieter Erasmus, head of the Eastern Province Agricultural Union, said training a sheepdog was no more difficult than training a human shepherd.
"Dogs have certain benefits," he said. "They don't strike, they don't complain, they do the job, and they're very loyal."
Erasmus and du Toit were speaking after a meeting between a SAAU delegation and Derek Hanekom, land and agriculture minister, over farmers' objections to the land tenure bill.
The SAAU leaders said the bill was causing rural job losses because land owners feared it would give anyone living on their property entrenched rights to remain.
Hanekom said the two sides had agreed to undertake nine days of intensive consultation to try to rephrase those sections that could have "unintended consequences".
"This bill is controversial and it's trying to address a very difficult issue," Hanekom said. "There isn't a simple answer or we would have come up with it a long time ago."
